rendered: The NFA hydroxide precursors must be coprecipitated within a narrow pH window: the document says the process coprecipitation window between 10 and 12[1]. The window is needed because aluminum hydroxides start precipitating at a lower pH than the others, while nickel and iron hydroxides precipitate beyond pH 6[2]. Simultaneous coprecipitation of nickel, iron and aluminum is hard because of differing solubility products (Ksp) of the resulting hydroxides, and the window was identified by analyzing the pH profiles of the individual constituent ions and the NFA material. In practice the reactor is run with NaOH added to maintain the pH to above 10[3], especially for nickel-rich cathodes. To make the powder, the outflow is The outflow from the reactor is filtered, washed, and dried[4] to obtain the hydroxide precursors, which are mixed with a lithium source (Li2CO3, LiOH, LiNO3, etc.) before calcinating[5] and calcined in an O2-rich environments at temperatures >600 °C[6]. The resulting NFA cathode powders are then cast into electrodes using a roll-to-roll slot-die coating process.
